status: frozen synthetic holdout for BNK-PDF-1 G9; sealed and committed before the product was run on any of its files
question: After the G8 reader fixes, made after seeing the G8 holdout (guards judged by proved glyph ink, a DR mark after its amount, touching date runs, typed cashbook amounts read by value), does bank-statement-native-1 read and reconcile statements from two further PDF writers it has never read, telling new stories within the same contract, with every eligible positive completed and no false automatic approval?

producers: WeasyPrint 70.0 with pydyf 0.13.0: an HTML and CSS paged-media engine that lays text out with Pango (HarfBuzz shaping, FriBidi ordering) and writes the PDF itself; each page is one HTML section, a right-to-left statement is laid out from the right by WeasyPrint, and a ligature's letters are named by the writer

MuPDF 1.28.5 through PyMuPDF 2.0 (Story): MuPDF's own HTML layout, HarfBuzz shaping and PDF writer; table columns sized by their content and laid out from the left whatever the direction, so the Arabic statement's columns are written in right-to-left order; Arabic drawn in reading order with presentation forms in the text layer
fonts: IBM Plex Sans Arabic (Arabic, many ligatures)
all from Fontsource npm packages, none a system font; the fonts given to MuPDF without the standard ligature feature
geometry: withdrawals and their total in dark red
a vector logo beside the bank name
a small raster logo above the bank name
the period's dates with their segments reversed in a right-to-left account line, as Chromium prints them in the foundation
changed.furniture: two banks in English and Arabic (Qasr Commercial Bank, Najd Investment Bank), document titles and accounts other than the foundation's, G6's and G8's
changed.references: references with a two-digit year (QCB260503001), with slashes (NIB/0601/001), with inner spaces on the statement only (FT 2607 1400), a cheque number (CHQ004417), one batch reference on two movements (BATCH-0216), letters and digits run together in an Arabic statement (NJ0301001)
changed.relationships: a business calendar: Sunday to Thursday, rent on the first business day, payroll by the 25th, a utility bill in mid-month, card settlements and transfers with the cashbook up to three days behind; cashbook entries dated before the period that clear in it, a cheque written four weeks before it was presented, profit credited and a fee charged by the bank only, two equal transfers against three equal payments in the same days, equal amounts three days apart without references, a payment booked in two halves under one reference, one batch reference twice on each side, value dates before and after the period, an account opened overdrawn that recovers, amounts a typed cell stores as a whole riyal or with one decimal
changed.text: descriptions that wrap where the writer breaks them, a description continuing at the top of page 9 of 29
changed.faults: the statement total of withdrawals 0.01 above their sum, page 2 declaring four pages where there are three, a balance carried forward from page 1 10.00 above the running balance
changed.cashbookXlsx: N02 as a typed XLSX from SheetJS (strings as formula-string cells), N10 as a typed XLSX from openpyxl; dates and amounts as numbers in both; every cashbook also as CSV

heldConstant: the contract's column headings, control-line labels and Page n of N footer, in English and Arabic
the account/currency/period line as one line
dates as yyyy-mm-dd, SAR with two decimals, thousands separators, the DR suffix for an overdrawn balance
a real text layer; no scanned page

independence.author: The same assistant wrote the product, the foundation, the oracle, the G6 and G8 holdouts, the G6, G7 and G8 fixes and this holdout, and knew the reader's rules when designing the stories. The variations are geometry, text and relationships the contract leaves open, chosen as what statements show; none was chosen to pass or to fail a rule. This is not a blind holdout: the stories and the writers are new to the product, the author is not.
independence.oracle: audit/bank-statement-foundation/oracle.py, unchanged: it reads the printed lines in the facts, the cashbook CSV and the contract, never recipe or intent, and imports nothing from the generator or the product. expected.py only runs it story by story with each story's own period.
independence.verifier: pdfminer.six, a PDF reader unrelated to the product's pdf.js, finds every printed line of the facts on its own row with all its values, every English description's words in order across the rows it wraps over, and every Arabic description whole on its row in reading order (verify.py, with its own self-test of 31 planted changes).
independence.generator: stories.py is a fourth lineage: a business calendar driven by a SplitMix64 generator; nothing is imported from the foundation's stories.mjs or from the G6 or G8 holdouts.
independence.drafts: While the stories and writers were drafted, their PDFs were read only with pdfminer.six and Poppler's pdftotext and pdftoppm, never with the product's reader.
independence.notTuned: The product was not run on these files, and no product code changed, between the start of G9 and the seal.

eligibility.why: Every statement stays inside the contract: its headings, labels, footer, line kinds, number and date formats and matching policy. The writer, font, table style, geometry, period, furniture and story are what the contract leaves open. The logos of N01 and N08 sit in the letterhead, apart from every line of text.

measures.reading: Every printed line read from the PDF equals the facts: kind, page, dates, reference, amounts, balances; descriptions and continuation text after NFKC and whitespace normalisation.
measures.result: The matching result, in the facts' keys, equals EXPECTED.json: automatic pairs, review groups with their reasons, both outstanding sides, timing, and held statements with their counts.
measures.capacity: Eligible positives whose result equals EXPECTED.json from upload through matching, save, restore and Excel in the browser.
measures.falseAutomatic: Automatic pairs that EXPECTED.json does not hold, over all twelve statements. Must be zero.
measures.held: A held statement is held whole, with the oracle's status, and nothing in it approved, suggested or called outstanding.
measures.refusal: A positive the product refuses, or holds without the oracle holding it, is a failed positive, never a correct abstention.

afterRun: Results are recorded as they come, with the commit they ran on. A fix made after seeing them turns this set into regression for that fix; a new claim of generalisation needs a new holdout.
